results.title: LiDAR Remote Sensing: A Powerful Tool For Precision Mapping
results.content: Drone-based LiDAR remote sensing is changing the game for both **government** and **commercial applications** as the need for quick, high-resolution mapping increases. # Role of Drones in LiDAR Remote Sensing. **Why Drones Are Ideal for LiDAR**:. * **Cost-Effectiveness**: Drone-based LiDAR considerably lowers operating costs and manpower requirements when compared to helicopter or fixed-wing aircraft surveys. Today’s drones are making **LiDAR remote sensing** faster, smarter, and more scalable than ever before by combining AI-powered flight planning with RTK/PPK technology. LiDAR becomes even more flexible when **mounted on drones**, which speeds up, secures, and lowers the cost of gathering high-quality data. # Benefits of LiDAR Remote Sensing with Drones. Professionals who require quick, precise, and comprehensive spatial data can benefit greatly from the combination of LiDAR technology and drones. LiDAR-equipped drones are perfect for engineering, land surveying, and environmental analysis because they can provide elevation and structural data with centimeter-level accuracy. Rapid deployment, shorter data collection cycles, and reduced operating costs are all made possible by drone-based LiDAR. While using drones for LiDAR remote sensing has many benefits, there are certain issues that organizations need to resolve to guarantee precise and useful results. Both technical piloting abilities and familiarity with geospatial data processing are necessary for operating a LiDAR drone. Advances in automation, data processing, and drone technology are influencing the direction of LiDAR remote sensing. In applications like mobile mapping, site inspection, and emergency response, newer drones are starting to allow real-time processing of LiDAR data onboard, allowing for real-time decision-making. **LiDAR remote sensing** is poised to become a commonplace tool for high-precision, scalable geospatial intelligence as drone regulations and technology advance. Drone integration has greatly increased the potential of **LiDAR remote sensing**, which has become a **fundamental component** of contemporary mapping and spatial analysis. **Drone-based LiDAR** provides unparalleled accuracy, versatility, and efficiency in a variety of industries, from obtaining centimeter-accurate terrain data to permitting safe surveys in hazardous conditions. LiDAR remote sensing using drones is no longer just the future; it is now the norm for precise, trustworthy geospatial intelligence, regardless of your field—construction, agriculture, mining, or environmental science. results.title: Considerations choosing a LiDAR drone for mapping | Routescene
results.content: Payload, flight performance (duration and speed), fuel type, type of drone (multicopter, Vertical Take Off and Landing or fixed wing) and whether you need Beyond Visual Line of Sight (BVLOS) operations should all be considered when selecting a drone. Here are our tips for choosing a drone to fly your UAV LiDAR system:. With short duration drones (15-20min) the number of flights and take-off and landings you need to do to cover a survey area will be much more than with a long endurance drone (3hrs), such as the Perimeter 8 from Skyfront. A 3 hour long endurance drone flying at 5m/s will enable you to survey 54 line kilometers in one flight. See our article on how we tested the flight time of the Skyfront drone carrying Routescene’s UAV LiDAR System at Skyfront’s test site in California. This is because drones need batteries that will provide high power to the props during take-off and yet the batteries need to be as light as possible to increase the UAV’s endurance. Routescene UAV LiDAR System mounted onto a battery powered drone. Hydrogen fuel cells are much heavier and larger than Li-Po batteries so this type of energy source is restricted to the larger UAVs. This means the Maximum Take Off Weight (MTOW) of the UAV may fall in a higher class of drone. The skill level required to fly a helicopter is much higher than for a multi-copter or fixed wing mapping drone, requiring a skilled and specialist pilot. For example, the number of power line kilometers that can be inspected and surveyed in one flight will greatly increase, making the BVLOS drone a more attractive and cost effective platform compared to the manned helicopter, which has a much higher operating cost. The primary consideration is the ability of the drone to lift the weight of the LiDAR equipment comfortably and fly for a required amount of time (this does depend on your application). In the near future we expect to see applications such as vegetation clearance for power lines being carried out by long-endurance drones operating Beyond Visual Line of Sight (BVLOS).

results.title: SPH Engineering and GreenValley International synchronize drone technologies for LiDAR data collection and processing – sUAS News
results.content: # SPH Engineering and GreenValley International synchronize drone technologies for LiDAR data collection and processing. Riga, Latvia – June, 2022 – SPH Engineering and GreenValley International partner combining their expertise to deliver drone software technologies for LiDAR data collection and processing. The companies align UgCS mission planning software and LiDAR360 data processing software to optimize the workflow with LiDAR data collected with a UAV. The partnership is ready to provide a full end-to-end software toolchain for airborne LiDAR applications. It includes flight planning and data collection (done with UgCS) and data processing (using LiDAR360), which are necessary for delivering meaningful results such as elevation models, terrain mapping and modelling, forestry scanning, and power line inspection. “Manual drone flight planning does not guarantee a stable flight. Automated mission planning using UgCS allows users to plan LiDAR surveys with adjustable corner radius and calibration segments, overcoming these issues and guaranteeing the results to be more accurate” describes Alvin QIU at GreenValley International. “We decided to test LiDAR360 upon the recommendation of one of our partners. We have evaluated multiple software packages for LiDAR data processing and found that LiDAR360 is the most universal and provides a good balance between user friendliness and professional results”, explains Alexey Dobrovolskiy, CTO at SPH Engineering. SPH Engineering (sph-engineering.com) is a global provider of UAV software solutions, integration services, consulting and custom development to expand drone applications. Its innovations support UAVs of different manufacturers and advance drone technologies for surveying, data collection, and entertainment. Partnering with renowned LiDAR sensor producers like RIEGL and Livox, GreenValley focuses on LiDAR and image fusion technology, specializing in lidar, UAV, SLAM, photogrammetry, and other technologies to achieve an accurate digital representation of three-dimensional space. GVI high-precision lidar scanning systems, such as LiAir (UAV/Fixed-Wing),.
